How wrong can you get beans on toast? Apparently, totally.

I asked when ordering if the toast would be buttered before the beans were put on and was told, yes it would.
And yes, I asked because that’s happened somewhere before.

After a decent wait out came two pieces of cold toast. Two patties of butter. One small ramekin of beans. I kid you not, we’ve entered the age of deconstructed beans on toast (or Beans Not On Toast).

I spread the beans to find they’d cover one slice of toast, and a third of the second slice.

I explained this to the manager and asked for some extra beans. My ramekin was taken and was then dumped back on the table with a “there you are”.

The beans must have been blitzed in a nuclear reactor to look how they did. Needless to say I didn’t eat them.

Before this little adventure, we’d been talking about bringing Dad out here for a treat. The setting is glorious!

My experience with Fairways Property Management at Broughton House has been extremely disappointing.

There have been ongoing issues with basic building infrastructure, including the intercom and lift, which have affected access and day-to-day living. I have also had safety and security concerns relating to the building, and I do not feel these were handled with appropriate urgency, transparency, or care.

Communication has been one of the biggest problems. In my experience, responses have been dismissive and unhelpful, with very little sense of accountability. As a resident, I expected clear communication, proper follow-up, and practical action. Instead, I felt that my concerns were minimised and that I was left to manage the situation myself.

A property management company should make residents feel that their building is being properly looked after. Unfortunately, my experience at Broughton House has been the opposite.

I would not recommend Fairways Property Management based on my experience.

I am only giving one star as I cant go into minus. This company should get an award for the most badly run management company in either Sheffield or South Yorkshire. As an apartment owner on The Dale it is embarassing seeing the state of disrepair this development is now in. Anyone thinking of either buying here or renting do yourself a favour and look elsewhere. The property managers are an absolute joke and are keyboard warriors who send emails but never achieve anything. The maintenance on this development is NON EXISTENT due to lack of funding apparently.

Fairways Management Sheffield is, without question, one of the poorest property management companies I have dealt with. I would strongly advise against purchasing a property under their management.

I have owned my apartment since 2017. At the time of purchase, I was assured that the communal areas would be redecorated. Nearly a decade later, this commitment has still not been fulfilled. The communal spaces remain in a consistently poor and neglected condition, with visible damage, including burn marks and deteriorating doors that are only occasionally and inadequately patched rather than properly repaired or replaced.

As an owner of multiple properties, including this apartment which I use as a base while working in elite sport, the contrast is stark. The wider area is excellent, yet the condition of the building creates an immediate and lasting negative impression. It reflects extremely poorly on both the development and its management.

While the disruption caused by COVID-19 may have been a reasonable short-term justification, it does not explain the continued lack of meaningful maintenance or improvement in the years since. The only recurring response appears to be superficial “deep cleans,” which do nothing to address the underlying structural neglect.

Communication and accountability are also major issues. Staff turnover is so frequent that there is no continuity in dealing with ongoing concerns, and it is rare to speak with anyone who has prior context or ownership of previous discussions. This results in a consistently frustrating and ineffective management experience.

Overall, the standard of management is unacceptable given the service charges being paid. There is a clear lack of care, follow-through, and responsibility, and the building continues to decline as a result.

Horrendous experience with Enviroskip Hire and do not recommend.

My in-laws, aged 70 and 77, hired a skip advertised as holding around 80 bags of waste. Before booking, photos of the driveway were sent over and we were assured access would be fine.

When the driver arrived, they were then told the skip wouldn’t fit on the drive, so it became a “load and go” arrangement instead. The driver himself was polite and pleasant, but it was never clearly explained that they would still effectively be charged the full skip price despite only a small amount being removed. They literally thought he was doing them a favour and taking the rubbish.

In total, approximately 15 bags and a single bed frame were taken — nowhere near the amount the skip was meant to hold.

What made the situation far worse was the attitude from the director, Lisa, when we raised concerns. The conversation was dismissive, unpleasant and completely lacking in professionalism or empathy, especially considering this involved elderly customers.

Had we been told from the start that the skip may not fit despite the photos provided, or that only a fraction of the waste would be removed while still charging full price, we would never have agreed to proceed.

Charging elderly customers full price for taking such a tiny amount of waste feels completely unjustifiable and considering this involves old aged pensioners, is absolutely shocking.

She eventually refunded £150, effectively charging £200 to take a car load of household waste, bedding, clothes & paper, which we could have quite easily done ourselves, for free!!!!!!

I would strongly advise against using this company.

I ordered £90.24 of goods in April 2026. The order was marked as delivered by the courier but never arrived. I contacted The Skinny Food Co the same day and made several follow-up phone calls in the days that followed. It took 7 days to receive a first response.

When they did respond, I was asked to complete a courier claim form and was told that resolution would be dependent on the outcome of the courier's investigation. This is not consistent with UK consumer law, under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, the retailer is responsible for delivery, not the courier. I flagged this in writing at the time.

After their own investigation deadline passed with no update or resolution, a replacement order was eventually sent after I chased them. That also failed to arrive. At this point I formally requested a refund. The response I received was a holding email and a 10% discount code.

The front gates of the development are also regularly broken (unlocked) and the main lift is often out of use. Due to recent bad weather, the roof of the Court has also leaked in certain areas of the building, rendering stairwells out of use.

I often saw fly-tipping in the surrounding area in which the development is situated (see picture) and smash-and-grabs from parked cars on the main road in the summers were a real problem. The local shop is also, from what the staff say, constantly dealing with armed robberies.

It should not be that hard for a tenant to receive a response to an email within a reasonable time-frame (and was not so with the previous management). Though I was prepared to give them the benefit of the doubt on the first few occasions that emails went unanswered or had unreasonable delays in response, this unprofessional level of communication unfortunately was commonplace and regretfully became expected. one_star_reviews.text:
I visited over the Easter period specifically to observe the “meet the bunnies” experience as I had prior concerns about rabbit welfare which I raised with the team in advance. I was disgruntled to pay £14.95 per person, but had to pay this to form a balanced opinion.

Before attending, I contacted the farm with a number of detailed, welfare-focused questions around how the rabbits would be managed during repeated public interactions. While I received polite responses outlining basic controls (rotation, supervision, limited handling), my wider concerns about cumulative stress, prey animal behaviour, and the suitability of this type of event were not meaningfully addressed.

Having now visited in person, I do not feel that this experience should have been run in any format. Rabbits are highly sensitive prey animals, and repeated exposure to noise, unfamiliar people, and handling throughout the day is inherently stressful, even if each individual interaction appears brief or controlled.

What was particularly disappointing is that there was a clear opportunity to take on board constructive feedback prior to the event. I had suggested more welfare-led alternatives and educational elements to promote responsible rabbit ownership, but these were not implemented. It gives the impression that the focus was on running a popular Easter attraction aimed at children interacting with “bunnies” rather than genuinely prioritising rabbits needs.

I cannot support or recommend experiences like this where animal welfare feels secondary to visitor engagement and profit.

Public holiday

I knew there was something not right with it though as puss would sometimes build up and seep out of it. After back and forth with ENT specialists for years i ended up having surgery this year to remove a cyst that was underneath all the scar tissue. Unfortunately this didn't work and i had to have another operation 5 months later as another smaller cyst had formed. Again this hasn't worked and the ENT specialist told me because i had my tonsils lasered years ago it didn't fully remove my tonsils and there is still some left and that crypts behind that means cysts develop. He is unwilling to touch it again as there is so much scar tissue now and i was told if i had just had a tonsillectomy from the start i wouldn't be having these problems now. This has left me with no options now but to live with it and i really regret getting my tonsils lasered by Mike Dilkes.

I have read the reviews on here and it seems a lot of other people have been through the same which is why i am leaving this review so other people don't have to go through what i have.

UPDATE! I have emailed Mr Dilkes to tell him about what I have been going through the past few years and the problems I still have and he just dismisses them as not his fault and blames the surgeon who has done 2 operations on me in 2025 to rectify Mr Dilkes 3 procedures that did not work on me. I used to come to Drayton Manor in the mid-90s as a kid and absolutely loved it. I’ve got really fond memories of the place, which is why it genuinely hurts to write this.

Sadly, it feels like the park has changed beyond recognition, and not for the better. Everything now feels monetised to within an inch of its life. £3.50 for a bottle of water or a can of pop is ridiculous, especially in the current cost of living climate. 60p for a sachet of ketchup is just embarrassing. Then there’s £12 parking on top, because apparently even leaving your car there is now a luxury experience.

The biggest issue, though, wasn’t just the prices. It was the overall state of the park and the rides. Several rides had technical issues throughout the day. We queued for ages for one ride, finally sat down, and were then told to get off because of a fault.

Similar issues happened elsewhere, with some rides running at reduced capacity or not running properly at all.

A lot of areas also looked tired and scruffy, like basic maintenance just isn’t a priority anymore. Some rides clearly need more than one member of staff operating them, because the checks and loading times take forever. It felt painfully inefficient.

What used to feel like a magical family day out now feels like shameless money farming with the bare minimum effort put back into the experience.

I really wanted to enjoy bringing my kids here and sharing the memories I had growing up. But after today, I honestly won’t be bringing them again.

A real shame, because this place used to mean something.

I booked this massage really looking forward to feeling relaxed and “chilled” afterwards, like I usually do after a deep tissue session. I asked for a medium to hard pressure as I’ve had many deep tissue massages before and generally tolerate firm pressure well, so I do understand the difference between therapeutic discomfort and excessive force.

Unfortunately, this experience crossed that line for me. The pressure used throughout most of the session felt far beyond what was manageable. I was tensing up constantly and at points felt close to tears, and I ended up crying afterwards. I left feeling distressed rather than relaxed.

What concerned me most was the lack of check-ins or adjustment during the treatment, despite how visibly my body was reacting. The pressure was only reduced after I eventually asked for it to be softer. In my experience, a good deep tissue massage should be responsive to the client’s body rather than pushing through sustained resistance.

There is also an important distinction with deep tissue work: if pressure causes the body to tense or go into “protection mode,” it becomes counterproductive, because the therapist can no longer effectively access deeper layers of muscle tissue. That’s part of why this felt unhelpful rather than therapeutic.

For me, there is a clear difference between effective deep pressure and pain that feels overwhelming, and unfortunately this experience felt much closer to the latter.

Never again.

We rented through the Penistone branch of Lancasters and found the experience very stressful overall.

At the start of the tenancy, we requested an inventory, but this was not provided. As no inventory was given, we documented the condition of the property ourselves, which provided some reassurance regarding the deposit. However, from a landlord’s perspective, this represents a lack of basic process and exposes both tenants and landlords to unnecessary risk.

When we moved in, the property was not in a suitable condition. There were areas where wallpaper had been stripped, plaster was missing from the walls, and rubble had been left on the floor. In addition, the property was advertised as unfurnished, but items such as a single bed and a freezer had been left behind.

We also experienced delays with essential repairs. The boiler was leaking and repeatedly losing pressure, and it took approximately two months for this to be resolved. In the meantime, we had to manage the issue ourselves, which we did not feel should have been necessary as tenants.

There was also an issue with an extractor fan which we were initially told would be an easy fix, but this was never resolved during our tenancy.

Communication was difficult throughout. It was challenging to get responses, and the only way we were able to make progress was by escalating matters to management. Even then, responses were unhelpful and did not adequately address our concerns.

It was only after raising the issues with a regulatory body that action was taken to bring the property to a liveable standard.

Having previously been a landlord, I understand the importance of proper documentation, communication, and ensuring a property is fit to live in from the outset. Unfortunately, this was not our experience.

We hope this feedback is taken constructively to improve standards for future tenants.

We were asked to leave a review for our experience with Lancasters on the day we picked up the keys. I did not feel like I could without retaliation while the tenancy was active. We primarily dealt with Daniel White and the agency's managing director, Kevin Crossfield.

We had a viewing where we were verbally informed the works on the house would be completed. They were not by the time we picked the keys up. Photos attached: incomplete works, visible debris, carpet still covered in plastic to protect from works, ladder left behind in a room, food rubbish still left in the fridge etc. The property needed hours of deep-clean by ourselves. On raising concerns, we were initially met with an understanding of the situation and an assurance to fix this quickly.

Nearly a month later of constant inspections for remedial work, constant emails, many phone calls of escalation, and formal complaint we managed to get into a position to be able to live in the house. We were told we couldn't cancel the tenancy as it is a fixed tenancy and so it was too late. We were then told it was our fault for wanting to move in on the date we wanted. We were also told we knew what the property looked like on viewing despite clear assurance the works would be completed prior. We were also blamed for being unreasonable that the property had only minor issues, despite the pictures attached. A whole month of rent felt wasteful.

We were also repeatedly informed that as agents they were only able to act on what the landlords can authorise, which is understandable but they were continuing to take commission from our rent hence also responsible.

Further problems with the house through the tenancy included: a delayed response to replacing an internal smoke alarm (1 month), a completely missed expired gas certificate where we were contacted nearly a month after the expiration to set a date at which point we had a response a month later to this. At this point we decided to move out and not continue to be involved further.

Any further evidence to this review would be available as they have all been neatly organised.

**[COMPLAINT] Zen Internet – Broken Promises, No Installation, No Internet, Zero Support**

I'm writing this post because I feel I have no other option left. After days of wasted time, broken promises, and an appalling customer experience, I want to warn others and hold Zen Internet publicly accountable. I will be sharing this post across every major UK forum, review site, and social platform I can find – because no one else should have to go through what I am currently experiencing before they make a decision about their broadband provider.

---

**Why I Chose Zen Internet**

I came across numerous glowing reviews of Zen Internet on forums like this one – praise for their reliability, premium service, and customer care. So when Virgin Media offered to renew my contract at £21/month for 1,000Mbps, I turned it down. Instead, I signed up with Zen Internet at £45/month for Full Fibre 900, trusting the community's recommendations. High-quality, stable broadband isn't a luxury for me – it's a necessity. I run a business from home, and my household relies heavily on connectivity, including multiple smart home devices.

---

**The Broken Promise That Started Everything**

I signed my contract with Zen in early March. Installation was confirmed for on or before 25th March – the exact date my Virgin contract was due to expire. Before committing, I specifically asked Zen's customer service: *what happens if installation isn't completed by the 25th?* I was given an explicit assurance – **repeatedly and emphatically** – that Virgin would NOT cut my service until Zen's installation was fully complete. I made sure to confirm this multiple times precisely because I could not afford to be left without internet.

At midnight on 26th March, Virgin cut my broadband.

---

**What Happened Next**

- **Customer service**: Nearly impossible to reach. Expect to wait upwards of two hours just to get through on the phone – completely unacceptable for any ISP, let alone one charging a premium.

- **Rescheduled to 30th March**: After finally getting through and spending more hours on hold, I was assured – again, with absolute confidence – that an engineer would attend on 30th March. I stayed home all day waiting. No one came.

- **Pushed to 1st April, then 2nd April**: After another exhausting round of calls, I was told the issue had been passed to their "Openreach" team and that I'd receive an update on 1st April. The moment I hung up, I received an email confirming the next update date had already been quietly changed to **2nd April**. Not a confirmed installation date – just another update. All responsibility has simply been passed along the chain.

---

**Their "Solutions"**

When I asked Zen what they would do to help me in the meantime – bearing in mind their error has left me with **no internet whatsoever** – here is what I was offered:

1. **"Buy your own SIM card."** Customer service told me that having no internet was a personal expense and entirely my problem. They would not assist in any way.

2. **A temporary hotspot** – which sounded promising, until they admitted they had **no stock** and could not tell me when any would be available. It could be tomorrow. It could be a week. It could be a year. Those were, genuinely, the words used.

3. **A chatbot** – which, like the phone line, requires you to queue and wait indefinitely regardless.

---

**The Current Situation**

As it stands, I have been without any internet connection for multiple days through no fault of my own. My business has been disrupted. My household is affected. I have spent an embarrassing number of hours on hold or chasing updates – time I will never get back. Every promise made has been broken. Every deadline has been missed. Every so-called solution has collapsed.

I was sold Zen Internet on the strength of this community's recommendations. I paid a premium price for what was supposed to be a premium service. What I received instead is, without exaggeration, one of the worst customer service experiences I have ever had.

Fidler & Pepper were our acting solicitors for both the sale and purchase. Our experience during the process was incredibly stressful and deeply frustrating and we would NOT recommend their services for the reasons below.

The process dragged from March 2025 through to September 2025 with significant and avoidable delays throughout.

Communication became a major issue. What started off well quickly deteriorated into days and often weeks without any updates, leaving us constantly chasing for basic information. Responses were reactive rather than proactive, and it was almost impossible to speak to anyone directly. Calls were repeatedly blocked by the receptionist, with callbacks rarely happening, adding to the sense of being completely unsupported during a time-sensitive transaction.

Searches were confirmed as complete on 1st May 2025, yet there was virtually no progress for at least three months. Even more concerning, critical enquiries regarding an oil leak and underpinning, issues clearly identified in the original searches, were only raised at the end of July, putting the entire chain at serious risk at a very late stage.

We were under constant pressure from the chain, with repeated threats that our buyers were close to pulling out due to the lack of progress from Fidler & Pepper. It became clear they were not only slow in responding to us, but were also ignoring communications from the buyers’ solicitors and estate agent, further escalating tensions and delays across the chain. There was certainly no sense of urgency.

Because of how long the process took, we were also at risk of losing our HSBC mortgage deal, which added significant financial pressure on top of an already difficult situation. We made a complaint which got to the escalation team, however it seemed they didn’t care about the situation at hand as there was still no movement. When it came to signing important documents, Fidler & Pepper sent legal documents as a Word document still with track changes and my name spelt incorrectly. We told them about it and the response was “just sign it, and we’ll correct it afterwards”. Shocking response from solicitors who are dealing with your legal documentation!

This lack of urgency, poor communication, and last-minute handling of key issues caused serious and unnecessary stress, not just for us but for multiple families involved.

Overall, this was an exhausting and highly stressful experience. We would not recommend Fidler & Peppers services and strongly advise those to choose their solicitors carefully and read reviews beforehand.

Very poor experience from start to finish.

I ordered business cards and foamboard prints on 19 April and paid for 24-hour dispatch, with delivery expected by 21 April. The order was not dispatched until Thursday evening and arrived Friday, several days late, with no proper explanation or apology.

Unfortunately, the quality of the items was also unacceptable. The business cards did not match the approved proof - they were visibly misprinted and miscut, leaving the design skewed. The foamboard prints were described as “100% ok” to PayPal once I escalated it; arrived with multiple issues including white spotting, streaking lines, uneven cutting, and noticeable colour differences compared to the proof.

After raising these issues, the seller agreed to arrange collection on 28 April and issue a refund. I confirmed availability, but no collection was arranged and all follow-up messages have been ignored.

I made several attempts to resolve this directly via email and phone before escalating further.

UPDATE:
After I left my original review, the business owner contacted me outside normal business hours and offered a full refund if I removed my review and immediately cancelled the chargeback I had raised with my bank. I explained that I was not comfortable cancelling the chargeback until a refund had actually been received, and that any amendment to my review would depend on how the matter was ultimately resolved. I was assured that the refund would be issued the following morning.

No refund was ever received.

In the week that followed, I received a number of calls from a withheld number. The calls stopped after I raised the business owner's name during one of those calls. Based on information available to me, I believe the calls may have been connected, and I have reported the matter to the police.

I stand by my review, which reflects my genuine experience as a customer. I will not be pressured into removing or altering a review in exchange for promises that were ultimately not honoured.

Absolutely dreadful experience from start to finish.

Their website and upload system feels like something dragged out of the 1990s, and because the upload process was unclear, I did exactly what any sensible customer would do — I followed up immediately by email, clearly stating:

“Please note the 2x banners are for different printed banners (both versions uploaded).”

Dean then personally replied:

“Received the uploaded and approved files”

So naturally, I assumed someone had actually read the email.

I had also paid EXTRA for their “File Assist Highly Recommended service for peace of mind”, which supposedly involves checking files and uploads before printing. Apparently “peace of mind” does not extend to reading basic instructions attached to the order.

Despite all of this, they still printed and shipped TWO identical banners instead of one of each design.

To make matters worse, their phone support is essentially non-existent. You call, it rings endlessly, then an automated message says they’re “busy speaking to other customers” before hanging up on you. No voicemail. No queue. No callback. I tried all the options — sales, existing orders, accounts — exactly the same result every time. Nobody answers.

Everything then had to be chased by email while I was trying to prepare for a major event.

When I complained, the response was essentially:

it was my fault,
the emails were irrelevant,
and because I’d clicked approve, nobody needed to actually read the instructions they’d already confirmed they understood.

Then came the cherry on top — an email from the company stating:

“Ahh ok, Isle of white isn’t UK mainland anyway…”

Firstly, it’s Isle of WIGHT.
Secondly, it IS classed as UK mainland by Royal Mail and most sane people capable of basic geography.
Thirdly, maybe don’t lecture customers about logistics when you can’t even spell the place correctly.

The overall tone throughout was dismissive, unprofessional and utterly lacking accountability.

Mistakes happen in printing — that’s life. But blaming the customer after explicitly confirming the instructions were understood, while hiding behind terms and conditions instead of simply admitting someone didn’t read an email, is pathetic customer service.

If you don't believe me, just try and call them to discuss your order.

Avoid.

Never will I ever take my dogs to this place again. I had to take one of my dogs to be put to sleep. It was heartbreaking just to take him. When we got there I couldn’t bring myself to go in so my husband took him. Almost two hours later my husband brought him back out so we could take him home for burial. Two hours! In that time my husband was made to wait with our dog amid everyone else even though we had phoned in advance to check a private room would be available. Once he got in to see the vet he was kept waiting again. When all was done he was left waiting yet again and had to leave our baby alone to go find someone to take payment so they could leave. So much messing about no thought given at all to our loss. Heartless horrible people.

I would not recommend The Pet Vet Rotherham.

Only weeks after our dog Dolly was last seen at this practice, a vet at another practice discovered a large necrotic abdominal mass within minutes of examining her. The mass was approximately the size of a large orange and required urgent surgery, despite Dolly having been examined at The Pet Vet only weeks earlier where no mass had been identified.

Histology later confirmed a large necrotising ovarian tumour together with severe chronic uterine disease including pyometra, indicating that the condition had been developing over time rather than appearing suddenly.

Dolly first presented with these symptoms in October 2025, yet the condition requiring urgent surgery was only identified in March 2026 after we sought a second opinion at another veterinary practice.

Given the size of the mass and the chronic nature of the disease later confirmed on histology, it was difficult for us to understand how this had not been identified earlier.

We fully accept that Dolly would ultimately have required surgery. However, had the condition been identified earlier she would not have had to suffer severe symptoms for such an extended period of time.

Dolly had been seen at the practice on numerous occasions between October 2025 and February 2026, and we also had several telephone discussions with the veterinary team during this time, as her symptoms continued without resolution.

During this period she received consultations, tests and multiple courses of antibiotics. Much of the focus during this time appeared to be on treating a suspected urinary tract infection, despite her symptoms continuing.

On a number of occasions I spoke directly with a senior vet about my concerns and was reassured that Dolly was likely fine and did not need to be seen again at that stage, despite the symptoms continuing.

The notes show that only an AFAST/TFAST abdominal ultrasound was performed. Despite advertising a 128-slice CT scanner for advanced imaging, this option was never discussed or offered and only a basic scan was used that cannot properly assess structures such as the ovaries.

Given that Dolly initially presented with severe bleeding from her vulva, it was extremely concerning to us that more advanced imaging available at the practice was never discussed.

In total we spent over £4,000 on Dolly’s veterinary care.

We raised our concerns directly with the practice and attempted mediation through the Veterinary Client Mediation Service, however the practice declined to take part.

Thankfully Dolly has now had surgery and is recovering well, but this experience was extremely distressing for our family.

Absolutely awful experience. I took my 9-year-old cat in a week ago with a blocked nose, watery eyes, breathing changes, and loss of appetite. Within minutes, they prescribed antibiotics and painkillers without much investigation. While there was some slight improvement, the medication actually reduced her appetite further.

At the follow-up, again within just minutes, my partner was told it “could” be cancer. No real evidence, no proper discussion—just immediately handed a sheet with extremely expensive scan options (around £2000), followed by the suggestion that if we couldn’t afford it, we could euthanise her that same day.

This was incredibly distressing. I had to leave work because my partner was so upset, and understandably so. It felt rushed, insensitive, and honestly quite shocking to jump to such a severe conclusion so quickly.

On top of that, the whole experience felt very “money, money, money.” A huge amount charged for what amounted to just a few minutes in the room, with little care, reassurance, or proper investigation. Instead, it felt like we were being pushed toward expensive procedures rather than being supported with thoughtful, step-by-step care.

Since stopping the medication, our cat has significantly improved—she’s eating, drinking, moving around more, and her symptoms have eased massively. We’ve since sought a second opinion, as this approach felt completely unreasonable.

It also raises questions when multiple cats in the same household have shown similar symptoms—jumping straight to cancer in that context makes little sense.

I dread to think how many pet owners have been through similar situations here, feeling pressured into expensive decisions or even considering putting their pets to sleep without clear justification.

Overall, this experience caused unnecessary stress, upset, and even loss of earnings. We’re incredibly grateful we didn’t rush into such a drastic and costly decision based on that advice.

Absolutely awful creature supposedly in charge of the receptionists at the front desk called ‘Natalie’. Horrible to deal with and extremely rude. We won’t be giving this place our business purely based on her bad attitude. Great way to put off new customers.

It’s worth mentioning we were surprised by the extreme mark-up on prescription items. We were charged around £50 for each item on our prescription for ear drops and ear cleaner. At the time of our first review, both of these items online are available for a total of £30. That’s £70 wasted on nothing but mark-ups. I would avoid purchasing anything from them that can be obtained online. We offered to return the items (sealed and still boxed) for a refund, but they don’t do this as it’s ‘against policy’. Fair enough, but good to know for future reference.

In regards to the encounter we had with the ‘Customer Experience Manager’. We walked in for our follow-up appointment and were completely ignored for several minutes as she was on the phone, with no acknowledgement of us at all we stood and waited, which is fine. We got talking to a couple with a puppy the same breed as our dog in the meantime.

After she was finished with her call, we told her we have an appointment that we had scheduled for 12:45pm. I misspoke at this point as I was looking at my phone for the time and almost said 1:45. She heard me say one and then looked for us on the system. Her already unwelcoming attitude completely changed at this point and she told us we had missed our appointment as it was 11:45am.

My partner and I are both professionals who monitor our calendars quite strictly and at our previous appointment had stood and entered our appointment into our phones separately at the point of making it with the receptionist at the time. The likelihood of us both entering it incorrectly is slim to none. Mistakes happen and I showed her my phone so she could see that’s what I had it down as. At this point her attitude went a step further as if she was playing up for the audience as the other couple were now in the queue behind us. She said ‘well you said 1 earlier and then changed your story, which is it?’ – which is an extremely odd and hostile thing to say in that setting. Rather than being impressed by her the couple behind us made eye contact with us and were equally as surprised by how hostile she was being toward us.

At this point I asked my partner if she ‘was for real’ as I was in disbelief that she was actually behaving like this and speaking with such a poor attitude after we had been nothing but polite.

We then shook our heads and asked when the next available appointment was. She asked us ‘Well, do you work?’ I informed her that it doesn’t matter either way, and asked for the next available appointment. She then questioned us again if we work. It took three attempts back and forth to get her to divulge the next appointment. We then entered it into our phones again and went to leave and she clearly sarcastically offered to write it down for us and made a show of making sure we were handed it on a card. This is normal in most settings but it was the way she insinuated that we couldn’t be trusted, was patronizing and made us walk back up to the desk for the card.

We contacted the place after leaving this review to check if the prescription we had already paid for was repeating and were told no. We then received an email from the personal work account of the person this review revolves around accusing us of being ‘abusive and derogatory’. We didn’t reply. We received another email previous to the reply by the MD here from the ‘area manager’ stating that as we’re abusive, they are withdrawing their services and instruct their staff to report this abuse to the police. The letter was as bizarre as our encounter in the branch as we were nothing but polite. We have at no point been abusive. We are the ones who felt attacked.

We now have a call with the MD to discuss after she reached out from this review. What an utter joke that call was.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with my experience. I underwent rhinoplasty to correct a noticeably crooked nose and a visible lump. While the surgeon did slightly reduce the lump from the profile view, the overall result is far from what was promised. One side of my nose was essentially left untouched, and it remains visibly uneven and crooked. I questioned whether he forgot about that side and even he seemed visibly surprised at the state of it.

The changes made were minimal to the point of being barely noticeable, especially considering the significant cost of the procedure. I expected a meaningful improvement, but instead I feel like very little was actually done.

What is even more frustrating is the lack of accountability during the follow-up. I was told that this was “the best that could be done,” which felt dismissive and did not reflect the concerns I raised. There was no willingness to acknowledge the unsatisfactory outcome vs what he had deemed a completely reasonable and achievable goal pre-op and he did not discuss potential solutions, not that I would trust him with any more money for a second operation.

I completely understand that, in many cases, achieving the desired outcome from rhinoplasty may require more than one procedure. However, I feel misled by the clear gap between what was promised and the actual result. If this outcome was a likely limitation, I would have expected that to be communicated transparently from the outset. An experienced surgeon should set realistic expectations and clearly explain what can and cannot be achieved, rather than agreeing to results that ultimately were not delivered.

Overall, this was a costly experience with disappointing results. I regret going ahead with this surgeon and would not recommend them based on my experience.

I had been with Fletcher Smith now part of James Hallam for many years and always renewed my commercial motor insurance without much question. However, I noticed that the premium was increasing significantly year after year, so I finally decided to shop around. Although I expected it to be time consuming, I’m very glad I did, as I ended up saving a substantial amount on my premium.

While speaking to other insurers, I was informed that my previous policy may not have provided the correct level of cover. That was quite concerning, as it made me question what would have happened if I’d needed to make a claim.

I contacted my previous provider directly to raise this issue and was told a manager would call me back after returning from annual leave. Three weeks later, I am still waiting for that call.

It’s clear to me now that switching to a reputable company has not only saved me money but also ensured that I am properly insured. My advice to others would be to shop around rather than automatically accepting renewal quotes you may be surprised at how much you can save.

I’ve had a pretty frustrating experience with Cuckoo Fibre overall, despite some positives.

To start with the good: when the connection actually works, the speeds are genuinely very good. Streaming, downloads, and general browsing are all fast and stable at times, which is what you’d hope for from a fibre provider.

However, the issues around everything else have really let it down.

Customer service has been a major pain point. It often feels like the support team doesn’t fully understand what’s being asked, even for relatively simple requests. On multiple occasions, I’ve tried to get straightforward changes made and it’s either taken far too long or hasn’t been done correctly at all.

A big limitation is the lack of control over the router. You can’t make basic network changes yourself — things like opening ports, changing the WiFi password, or even renaming your network. This is incredibly restrictive, especially if you have smart home devices, gaming setups, or anything that requires port forwarding or custom configuration. Most providers allow at least some level of user control, so this feels unnecessarily locked down.

I’ve also had ongoing issues with devices struggling to connect reliably. There have been multiple engineer visits, and while they’ve confirmed there is a problem, no one seems able to identify the root cause. To make matters worse, the engineers aren’t directly employed by Cuckoo, so there’s a bit of a disconnect in accountability and follow-up.

On the administrative side, things haven’t been much better. I submitted a subject access request over 2.5 months ago and am still waiting for a response, which is well beyond expected timeframes. Formal complaints also seem to disappear into a void — I’m told responses have been sent, but I’ve never actually received them.

In summary, while the raw internet speeds are strong, the lack of router control, poor customer support, unresolved technical issues, and slow (or nonexistent) responses to formal requests make this a difficult service to recommend.

SDL were instructed by YBS to complete the valuation of our property, and we paid £229 to cover the cost of a level two homebuyer survey.

The Homebuyer Survey should include a visual inspection of all major features including ceilings, roof, walls, and bathrooms, as well as permanent outdoor buildings and features including roofing, pipes, gutters, walls, windows, and doors.

To say it was a waste of money is an understatement.

They gave our main roof a condition rating of 2, stated there were a few broken tiles and some which has been replaced. After a few broken tiles fell onto our drive, a roofing contractor told me that the condition of the roof from ground level inspection alone was appalling. Upon greater inspection we had over 50 broken tiles, some tiles glued together with adhesive, guttering that was filled with rubble and broken tiles, and ridge tiles being held in place by friction alone. Our roof should have never been given a good or satisfactory rating and is in fact in need of urgent repair. We have since had to fork out over £9,396 for a new main roof. There goes the bathroom renovation.

We then discovered that the roof on the extension of the property (given a condition rating of 1) had the incorrect tiles installed for the pitch of the roof. Again, a qualified (and decent surveyor) would have been able to make this conclusion from eye level. It's a matter of time before damp and leakage issues occur through the VELUX windows because of the pitch, and we are looking at over £6000 to have this roof re-pitched and replaced too, aswell as over £1000 for new VELUX windows.

Not to mention, the surveyor completely missed a hole in the side of our exterior wall, from an old soil pipe. We are again, having to fork out over £1,000 to get this fixed and we don't know if further damp issues are going to arise.

We would not have purchased the property had SDL's survey been accurate. I requested the site notes and photographs and SDL refused to release them (which is one, illegal as we paid for the service, and two either demonstrates that the photos show that the damage was there or no sufficient photographs or site notes were taken by the individual who inspected the property).

All they have been prepared to offer us was a £250 'good will' gesture which covers some of what we paid for the survey - nothing more.

I also reported them to their governing body. But as their terms and conditions state sometimes mistakes are made and things are missed - they legally completely get around situations like ours.

As first time home buyers we have been unable to move into the property until building work is completed and it has shattered our experience of buying our first home.

Avoid SDL at all costs. Just get a builder, electrician & roofer you trust to inspect your property so you know exactly what you’re getting yourself into.

Hero Man & Van made the usual stress of moving day a complete nightmare due to their numerous failings and have refused to take any accountability, to the point where I had to raise a dispute with my bank to get some of my money back.

The ‘package’ I paid for was £545 for 2 men and 1 Luton box van, for 4 hours. I was explicitly clear in all my correspondence that I needed help with bulky items only, as I had plenty of helpers/vehicles on hand to move boxes and smaller items. I had also moved the year prior, so I knew that 1 van would be sufficient.

On the day, I was informed there was an hour delay, which I was able to accommodate. In hindsight, this seemed to give them the green light to mess me about, because after that initial call, no one contacted me again and I had to keep calling to find out what on earth was going on. Each time, I was told they were an hour away, and each time, no one turned up.
I was moving out of a rental property which had a tenant moving into it that day, so having to repeatedly call an increasingly disgruntled landlord about MORE delays was immensely stressful.

Almost 3 HOURS later, 3 men, with 2 vans turned up.
The second van (I was not told about and did not consent to) caused disruption to the narrow cul-de-sac, meaning neighbours had to move off their drives to accommodate it.

Two of the men were pleasant and got on with the job, but the third man, who I believe was a temp, thought it was appropriate to stand and brag about how much money he was making that day and make sexist comments about my ability to pack up an entire house by myself - ‘you must be strong, it’s nice to see a woman doing something useful for a change’.
Unsurprisingly, he was later seen being heavy-handed with my belongings.

The men traipsed mud throughout the ground floor of the rental (despite there being back garden access) moments before the landlord was due to arrive, which put my deposit in jeopardy.

Within 24hrs I reported a broken tv plug and addressed that the job had been completed in less than the 4 hours I had paid for. I was instantly dismissed, despite being told when I booked that ‘if it can be done quicker, we’ll look after you’ i.e. refund you the extra (see email screenshot).

The job was completed in 2 hours, and I was being charged for 4. I was charged £545 for 2 hours.

For weeks the company invalidated me, before my bank stepped in and got me the partial refund I was due.

I realised after unpacking that I also had dents in white goods, smashed crockery and missing garden items. My washing machine, which was new, now makes an unsettling rattling noise.

I’d recommend not signing anything until you’ve fully unpacked and checked over your belongings - they tried using this against me in my dispute (and again in their response below!) stating that because I signed, I was ‘happy with the service’. Unbelievable! It seems to be their way of capitalising from the stress/chaos of moving day.

How a company handles complaints around its failings reveals its values and priorities and is a true representation of its character. The issues I raised throughout this ordeal were either met with dismissal or ignored entirely.

EDIT - to further highlight the true character of these people, the response below continues to make false claims.
I have now attached a screenshot of the email exchange which addresses the bizarre claim that I was ‘adamant I wasn’t paying from the beginning’ (?) Literally shows me acknowledging a price difference compared to what a friend was quoted…

The best lie has to be that I was offered a partial refund for the ‘inconvenience’. At NO point have I been offered a refund, hence being forced to raise a dispute with my bank. To state that they ‘won’ the dispute and then admit they later gave me a refund is just laughable - they were ordered to give me a refund based on the evidence I provided.

The regular excuse was they could not phone an international phone number, despite me only providing a UK number.
More concerning was an error in the purchase price recorded on my file. I had provided the correct purchase price from the outset in the initial paperwork and also discussed the figures by phone before instruction because the purchase included a discount. Despite this, the incorrect price remained on their system and was only identified at completion, which meant I had to arrange additional funds at very short notice.
During the complaints process, the firm maintained that I had originally provided the wrong figure, but they were unable to provide evidence to support that assertion when asked. I found this disappointing given that I held documentation showing the correct price had been supplied from the beginning.
They acknowledged some shortcomings and offered a goodwill payment. However, I did not feel this fully reflected the stress and inconvenience caused.

Update:
The response below does not match any previous communication from LPL. This is a new reason that has not been presented prior to this review and will be further communicated to the regulators to highlight the inconsistencies in their account.

If you value your sanity, your personal data, or basic human communication, I’d recommend avoiding this company like it’s offering free hugs during a zombie apocalypse.

From start to finish, the entire process was an Olympic-level disaster. Calling my case handler? Impossible. Requesting callbacks? Apparently just a fun decorative feature on their website. Emails? Oh, they do reply… eventually… usually after you’ve sent enough follow-ups to qualify as a part-time stalker.

My case handler, Halima, seemed deeply committed to the exciting corporate philosophy of “ignore the client until they lose the will to live.” To be fair though, this appeared to be less of an individual talent and more of a company-wide mission statement.

As a first-time buyer, I was absolutely thrilled when my purchase was delayed by SIX MONTHS — so close to collapse that the seller nearly walked away. Nothing says “welcome to homeownership” quite like constant stress and the very real possibility of becoming homeless before you even get the keys.

But wait, there’s more.

During the process, they accidentally sent my bank statements and passport copies to a third party. Did they notify me? Of course not. The THIRD PARTY had to tell me. To this day, I have no idea who else may now have my personal information floating around like confetti at a data breach parade.

Then, months after completion, the managing company contacted me about unpaid service charges from before I even owned the property. Apparently checking outstanding balances was simply too ambitious a task. So naturally, I got stuck paying someone else’s debt. Love that for me.

And finally — because every comedy needs a grand finale — a few months ago they mailed me TWO original marriage certificates belonging to complete strangers. Spoiler alert: I’m not married. I emailed them to let them know about their mistake, partly because I’m a decent human being and partly because I assume those people may someday want to legally separate. Unsurprisingly, I never received a response.

Ironically, their response to this review was the quickest I’ve ever heard back from them. Sadly, instead of replying to the actual email I sent warning them they had mailed me marriage certificates belonging to complete strangers, they simply informed me that my case was “from 2024” and that they’ve “improved their service since then.”

Bold strategy.

Especially considering I’ve attached a photo of the certified letter THEY sent me in FEBRUARY 2026 containing said random strangers’ marriage certificates. Nothing screams “we’ve improved” quite like continuing to breach client confidentiality years later with the enthusiasm of a company running a data leak loyalty scheme.

At this point, I’m honestly just waiting for them to accidentally send me someone’s kidney transplant paperwork and a Tesco Clubcard application.

I am extremely dissatisfied with the service I have received from this law firm.

I have been in the process of purchasing a property for over five months, and my solicitor has consistently caused unnecessary delays. Key documents were not properly reviewed, and even basic details such as the purchase price and related calculations were repeatedly recorded incorrectly across multiple documents. In practice, we have had to review everything ourselves and send corrections for them to amend.

What concerns me most is not only the errors we identified, but the possibility of further mistakes that may have gone unnoticed and could surface later.

Communication has been particularly poor. For almost every email or request we have sent, we have had to follow up multiple times before receiving any response — often several follow-ups. Responses are slow, and at times absent altogether. There was also a period where our solicitor went on leave without informing us in advance or ensuring that someone else would take over the case, which further delayed the process.

These ongoing delays have now put our purchase at risk, with the seller considering putting the property back on the market.

Overall, the level of care, diligence, and communication has fallen far below expectations. What should have been an exciting milestone — purchasing our first home together — has instead become a very stressful and disappointing experience.

Even writing this review, I feel concerned about potential repercussions on our case, which unfortunately reflects the level of trust and confidence we currently have.

I instructed Reed Roper T/A LPL in March 2025 to staircase my shared ownership property and this completed in June 2025.

I have since sold the property and entered a chain.  During the preparation of the sales pack, my current solicitors discovered that LPL hadn't updated the Land Registry.

I contacted LPL by phone seven times to raise this issue and get it rectified. They admitted they had forgotten to submit the application and said they would now send it and request it be expedited.  I asked for this to be put in writing to provide to my buyers however they refused.

Mistakes can happen and I understand that, but how a firm handles and rectifies them is crucial. LPL has failed to take responsibility and failed to communicate / be transparent.

As a direct result, my buyers have now pulled out of the sale.

I strongly recommend researching LPL thoroughly before instructing them. In my experience, they lacked communication, transparency, and accountability — all essential qualities in a solicitor.

•	Working from home has been directly impacted due to unreliable service

Despite raising this with support, resolution has been slow and communication inconsistent, including being cut off during support calls and the technical team contacting the wrong person.

I was previously provided with written confirmation that I could exit without penalty within the initial period if the service did not perform as expected. Based on current performance, the service is not meeting that standard.

At this stage, I am giving Gigaclear a final opportunity to resolve the stability and performance issues this week. If this is not achieved, I will be terminating the service.

This remains a consistent theme — initial failures, followed by reactive fixes, but ongoing difficulty delivering a stable and reliable service.

Following escalation to the Customer Resolutions Team, Gigaclear has now proposed:
•	Honouring the original pricing
•	Three months’ free service

•	Direct case handling to oversee installation

The proposal represents a fair commercial reset and protects me financially moving forward, although it does not fully address the historic disruption experienced over two failed attempts across two years.

I have requested written confirmation of installation safeguards and contract terms before proceeding.

If the installation is completed successfully and commitments are honoured, I will update this review accordingly.

For now, this is a “cautiously proceeding” position.

Absolutely shocking experience with ADT.

I recently moved into a property with an existing ADT alarm system and contacted ADT because the Stay mode is not configured properly. When Stay mode is activated, the kitchen and sitting room sensors still trigger the alarm, making the feature basically useless while we are inside the house. All I wanted was for the front door sensor to be active in Stay mode.

Instead of offering a sensible solution, such as a one-off engineer visit or remote configuration change, I was told that because there is no active account at the property, ADT will not assist unless I take out a new contract. I was advised this would be a 3-year contract, cancellable after 18 months, just to deal with what appears to be a basic settings issue.

That is ridiculous. I am not asking for a new system, new equipment, or ongoing monitoring. I simply wanted an existing alarm system configured so it could actually be used properly.

This experience has completely put me off ADT. I will be replacing the ADT system with one I can control myself, rather than being locked into a long contract just to change basic settings. My previous Yale alarm allowed me to configure this myself without any of this hassle.

Based on my experience, I would not buy an ADT system, I would not recommend ADT to anyone, and I would actively warn others to think very carefully before getting tied into their products or contracts.

one_star_reviews.text:
I attended their Ready, Set, Bloom event here and as stall holders, this was one of the worst event experiences we’ve had.

The event was severely lacking in organisation and promotion. Footfall was practically non-existent—only friends and family of other stall holders attended. There was no clear signage for the event, and even finding the farm itself was difficult, which only made the situation worse.

In the lead-up, communication from Lexy raised concerns, with repeated mentions of financial struggles and requests for further support. Stall holders were also encouraged to “invest” in Honey Nook C.I.C with promises of shelf space in a farm shop and access to exclusive events. However, there was no visible shop on site, and this has not been delivered as expected.

Following the event, several stall holders requested refunds for the £15 shop investment. These requests appeared to be ignored, and shortly afterwards Lexy left the group chat. To date, no refunds have been received.

On the day itself, there was no effort to meet, greet, or support stall holders. While poor turnout can happen, the complete lack of acknowledgement or apology from the organisers, including Bridget, was incredibly disappointing. Instead, stall holders were told to pack up early at 2pm, despite the event being advertised until 4pm.

Basic facilities were also not adequate, with no proper access to toilets, running water, or handwashing facilities.

Overall, a very frustrating and disheartening experience that left many people out of pocket. Based on this experience, we would strongly recommend others think carefully before committing to events or any financial involvement here.

I agreed to purchase a property marketed by Richard Watkinson and was explicitly informed at the time of my offer that there was no onward chain with the sellers purchase, with an expected completion date of end of February 2026.

I was also told that the sellers’ onward purchase was already built, ready to move into, and that they were even buying furniture for it—further reinforcing that there would be no delays.

Based on this, I proceeded in good faith—spending over £1,000 on expedited searches and surveys to meet the proposed timeline, and making personal arrangements accordingly.

However, after several months, I was informed that there was in fact a chain involved. From that point on, I was given a series of inconsistent and changing completion dates (June, then May, then August), with no clear or reliable communication.

On 1st May 2026, I was finally told that the chain had collapsed entirely and the property was no longer in a position to be sold.

As a direct result of relying on the information provided, I have incurred significant financial costs and have now been left without accommodation and effectively homeless.

This situation suggests that Richard Watkinson either failed to properly establish the chain status at the outset or communicated inaccurate information throughout the process. I would strongly advise others to steer well clear of these agents as they are clearly incapable of providing a service which should be standard by an established estate agent

My mother and father kept their wills with HSBC, which unfortunately now means dealing with the Co-op. After losing both parents in quick succession, I found myself navigating what can only be described as probate-themed endurance training.
First, I was confidently informed by one member of staff that the Co-op were the sole executor. They were not. Minor detail, apparently.
I then endured an hour-long conversation with a solicitor that felt less like legal advice and more like being cornered by someone trying to sell me a timeshare. At one point I genuinely asked if she was reading from a script. Judging by the pauses, I suspect the answer was yes.
The quote they eventually produced was so spectacularly inflated that solicitors I know through work looked at it with the sort of expression usually reserved for natural disasters and lottery winners.
I asked them to renounce and allow me to act as sole executor. Since then: complete silence. I’ve tried calling repeatedly and am currently 17 minutes into another hold queue while typing this. Last week I gave up before the music achieved permanent residency in my brain.
Their will-writing service may well be excellent. But before signing up, spare a thought for the relatives who’ll eventually have to deal with the company afterwards. Alternatively, if you possess a particularly dark sense of humour, appoint them as joint executor alongside someone you actively dislike.

29 minutes and I give up.... again

Update… Co-op is the joy that just keeps on giving. 🎻
For the last few weeks I’ve been trying to get the deeds of renunciation so I can apply for probate. According to several different people, I’d already been sent an email explaining everything I needed to do. Incredible really, considering this mystery email seems to exist only as folklore within the company.
I tried phoning, which mainly involved listening to hold music so often I’m now considering adding it to my Spotify Wrapped. I emailed the solicitors I originally dealt with, only to be told I needed to contact the department directly… while not actually being given the email address for the department. Perhaps they wanted to spice things up with a little detective work.
After enduring yet another concert of soul-destroying hold music, I finally reached what I believe may be the only competent person in the organisation. Diane from Renunciations informed me that I hadn’t received the details because someone had sent them to the wrong email address. The incompetence is honestly breathtaking. At this stage I’m less applying for probate and more starring in a low-budget administrative thriller.
Anyway, Diane deserves a pay rise. She’s the only person I’ve spoken to at Co-op who appears to know her job and, revolutionary concept, treated me like an actual human being.
So hopefully one day I will actually receive the details so I can begin battling the probate system itself. Until then, all I can really say is: don’t use this company unless you actively despise your surviving relatives.

one_star_reviews.text:
I visited Chole over a year ago for help correcting eyebrows that had been poorly done by another practitioner. They were asymmetrical, and my natural brow tails had been removed and replaced with PMU—something I had never requested and found very distressing.

Chole reassured me that she could improve the shape while keeping the result natural. I was very clear that I did not want darker or bold brows and was reassured this would not be the outcome. Based on this, I chose correction rather than full removal.

Although the shape was slightly improved, the brows healed much darker and more unnatural than I had wanted, which was exactly what I had hoped to avoid. I therefore chose not to proceed with the top-up appointment. At the time, I sent a polite message saying that overall she had done a good job but that I did not wish to continue, mentioning that I didn’t like the look of having no hair in the tails. In reality, my decision was due to the brows healing far bolder than I had asked for. Unfortunately, I did not receive a response.

More than a year later, I have now undergone my ninth removal session. Including the original treatment, I have spent around £1,000. This has been one of the most stressful and upsetting experiences I’ve had.

My advice to others would be to choose your practitioner very carefully and to seriously consider full removal rather than correction. I made the same mistake twice and paid for it—both emotionally and financially.

Update: At the start of the healing process, my brows did look improved overall, although I did feel they appeared extremely dark. I wasn’t too concerned at that stage, as I understood that brows typically lighten and soften significantly over the six-week healing period.

However, by the end of the six weeks, there was very little change. The colour didn’t fade as expected, and the brows still look overly saturated and blocky in appearance, which was extremely disappointing.

Chloe did explain that there were limitations to having my brows redone. However, my main concern was the risk of them becoming over-saturated. She reassured me that this would only happen after many sessions over a number of years, which made me feel comfortable proceeding.

Had I been made aware at any stage that the result could look overly saturated and blocky, I would not have gone ahead with the procedure.

The reason I didn’t contact Chloe immediately was because I first sought a consultation with a laser removal company. They advised that the discolouration above my brows, which I was concerned about, was actually residual ink still in the skin.
In contrast, Chloe suggested it was likely scarring and mentioned that she could offer a tattoo camouflage service to cover it, at an additional cost of £300. The laser clinic carried out a patch test, which successfully lifted the pigment completely.
This experience unfortunately made me lose confidence in Chloe’s assessment, as well as in her overall service and expertise.

I don’t believe this review is influenced by any wider issues; it is specifically based on my personal experience. My concern is that the service and advice provided did not resolve the initial problem and instead resulted in a worse overall outcome.

I don’t usually leave reviews, but this experience deserves to be preserved for future generations as a cautionary tale.

We collected our order ourselves, got all the way home, opened the bags, and realised the order was completely wrong. Somehow, what should have been a simple burger order looked like the kitchen had blindfolded someone and told them to grab random items. Missing wraps, wrong meals, extras we never ordered — honestly I was surprised there wasn’t a toaster in the bag as well.

So we rang up to explain the situation, expecting a quick apology and for the correct food to be delivered out to us. Instead, we were told they “couldn’t deliver” to our address. Which was interesting considering they apparently do offer delivery, and we’d only just been there minutes before. The whole conversation felt less like customer service and more like someone trying to improvise excuses in real time.

The woman manager we dealt with had absolutely zero people skills and communicating with her was painful from start to finish. Every question seemed to create more confusion, and instead of trying to solve the issue, it felt like we were being argued with for daring to want the food we actually paid for. I’ve had smoother conversations with automated parking machines.

In the end, we had to drive all the way back again to collect the correct order ourselves. By this point we’d spent more time travelling backwards and forwards than some people spend commuting to work.

Now to be fair, while we were there the second time, one of the delivery drivers who actually worked for the company was genuinely brilliant. Really friendly bloke, and he overheard the situation and said he absolutely would have delivered the replacement if he’d been asked to. So the nicest and most helpful person involved turned out to be the delivery driver standing there wondering why nobody had just sent him out in the first place. Someone give that man a raise immediately.

The food itself, once we finally got the right order, was alright. But by then the experience had become such a saga that eating the burgers felt more like the end of a difficult quest than dinner.

Such a shame as we have eaten here before and it’s been good, just shows how important a proper manager is within a business !

Overall, if you enjoy burgers served with confusion, unnecessary mileage, and a side order of excuses, this is definitely the place for you.

would not recommend this company based on my experience.
We hired them for an international move from London to Spain and paid for the delivery service in full in advance. The final amount also ended up being higher than the original quotation, with additional costs added during the process,  future customers: confirm every possible extra charge clearly in writing before agreeing to the service.

Before the delivery, we clearly explained that we were not in Spain and asked to be informed properly about the confirmed delivery date and time so a family member could be available to receive the boxes.
On the day of delivery, another driver/person (that we had not been informed about) attempted the delivery using a different UK phone number. Because the number was unknown, our family member did not answer the calls immediately. We were also not properly updated beforehand as requested.

Half hour later we realized the calls were related to the delivery and contacted the company, the driver had already taken all the boxes back to another city.
After this communication failure, we were asked to pay an additional €70 to finally receive belongings that had already been fully paid for.
In the end, we paid the extra amount simply to avoid more stress and delays, but the whole process was poorly coordinated and very frustrating.
The delivery itself was eventually completed, but the communication, organization and customer support experience were disappointing.

If you hire this company, make sure:
* all costs are confirmed in writing,
* you ask specifically about possible extra charges,
* all delivery contacts are clearly identified beforehand,
* and delivery coordination is confirmed step by step.

Unfortunately, our experience was stressful and far more expensive than expected.

Avoid This Dealership Unless You Want an 8-Month Legal Battle Over a Faulty Car
​If you are a car lover, please read this warning before stepping foot onto this forecourt. This dealership appears to hunt for highly desirable, rare specification vehicles to bait enthusiasts into buying cars that suffer from severe, inherent defects.
​I bought a beautifully specified L461 Range Rover Sport in a very rare Blue on Tan combination. Unfortunately, the stunning specification was a mask for a vehicle that was completely unfit for purpose and plagued by catastrophic water ingress. For months, this vehicle suffered from an ongoing water ingress defect where water continually flooded the rear boot lining and cabin floorboards, destroying the interior and threatening the complex electrical systems.
​The vehicle quality was entirely matched by the appalling, lazy, and utterly unprofessional customer service provided by the staff:
​Ryan & Dan: Unbelievably incompetent, took 30 minutes between several chats to his director for price negotiation, i almost walked out, and should have.
​Tom (Director): When these severe water ingress concerns were raised, Tom chose to entirely bury his head in the sand. His attitude was effectively to tell me "good luck" with a bad car, trying to call my bluff by forcing me to fight through my financial institution to get any semblance of justice.
The Delusion of Grandeur:
During a phone conversation, Tom personally told me that he aims for this dealership to be in the same league as prestigious, highly respected independent specialists like Alexanders Prestige and Redline Specialist Cars. If you want a laugh, go read the reviews for those long-established businesses, then look at how this company’s reviews are plummeting. True specialists protect their reputation at all costs and treat car lovers with respect. By dragging down the standards of the independent specialist market with lazy, predatory business practices, Tom and his team are giving genuine luxury dealers a bad name. They are not even in the same stratosphere as the reputable brands they claim to emulate.
​The 8-Month Battle and the Financial Verdict:
They thought I would roll over and accept a flooded luxury vehicle. They were wrong. I initiated a formal dispute through the finance provider, Black Horse.
​Following a 8-month ordeal, Black Horse officially sided with me. The bank’s explicit conclusion was that this supplying dealership provided a vehicle that was not of satisfactory quality and completely unfit for its purpose, and dangerous for use. Black Horse ordered a full buyback of the vehicle, forcing this dealership to take action for the defective car and refund my hard-earned money.
​Tom and his team should be utterly ashamed of how they treat consumers who spend vast amounts of money at their establishment. They count on you loving the car's spec so much that you will still trust them. Do not fall into their trap.
​I won my case, the bank exposed their practices, and they were legally forced to buy the vehicle back—but no consumer should have to endure an 8-month battle just to get a legal remedy. Buy from anyone else.

My experience with Trigglets Estate Agents was very poor. Communication was frequently slow and, in my view, fell below the level of professionalism I would expect from a letting agent, making even routine matters unnecessarily difficult.

The most serious issue arose at the end of my tenancy. I was presented with proposed deductions from my bond that, in my opinion, were excessive and did not reflect fair wear and tear. I found these charges difficult to justify based on the condition of the property and felt they were disproportionate. Fortunately, I was able to appeal the charges and the amount they claimed, was reduced.

Overall, the process did not feel transparent or handled in a fair and balanced way. Based on this experience, I strongly advise tenants to take detailed photos of every room, carpet, and wall at both check-in and check-out. Also ensure any prospective tenant thoroughly checks for accuracy, and signs, the check-in and check-out documents - this wasn’t offered to me, and I felt the charges proposed in my case, were punitive.

This review reflects my personal, distressing experience, so I would urge others to keep thorough records, scrutinise any proposed deductions carefully, and challenge anything they believe is unreasonable.
