one_star_reviews.text:
Over the time our child attended this nursery, we unfortunately had a number of concerning experiences that ultimately led us to lose confidence in the care being provided.

One of the most worrying incidents for us involved our child being given a food we had specifically asked the nursery to avoid due to a previous reaction. There were also occasions where when looking on the daily diary on the famly app, our child had not been changed for almost 5 hours and when this was bought to the nurseries attention, the reason given to us for this happening was due to the lack of communication between staff. We also experienced limited communication at pick-up times regarding our child’s day and development.
We also raised a safeguarding concern during our time there which, from our perspective, was not handled with the level of urgency or reassurance we would have expected. This was something we felt needed to be escalated further at the time and took it upon ourselves to contact Ofsted. These examples contributed to our overall concerns. When visiting the nurseries Ofsted page you can see there has been 2 ‘concerns - actions taken’ one in 2022 and one in 2025 which we feel like parents should know.

The nursery environment often felt busy to us, and at times we felt the space appeared crowded. In our experience, this sometimes made the setting feel less calm than we would have hoped. On occasion at pick-up, it appeared to us that some staff were not actively engaging with the children but sat talking amongst themselves.
The outdoor areas, particularly for the under-2s, felt limited in terms of space and equipment. During our initial visit, trips and outings were mentioned; however, in our experience, these did not happen frequently during the time our child attended.
We also had some concerns about general upkeep. For example, during winter we noticed bin bags stored next to the bins at the gates of the outdoor play area, which we personally did not expect in a childcare environment. We are aware the nursery’s food hygiene rating has changed, which may be something prospective parents wish to look into for themselves.

A large part of our dissatisfaction relates to communication and management. During the initial show-round, we found the manager to be warm and reassuring. However, once our child started, our experience of communication was more limited. At times we felt our questions or requests were not fully addressed, and when we raised concerns, we did not always feel listened to or reassured. This left us feeling uncomfortable raising further issues as we were made to feel like we were the problem.

That said, we did have positive experiences with the Deputy Manager Becky and the admin Kelly, who we found to be helpful and approachable when we needed support.

It’s disappointing to write this review, as we understand the nursery previously had a strong reputation. However, based on our experience, we felt that standards of communication and overall care did not meet our expectations. We hope this feedback is taken constructively, as every child deserves a safe, attentive and well-managed environment.

*EDIT* After reading the ‘response’ aimed at anybody reading and not ourselves we would like to clarify,

Our child remained in this nurseries care for 4 sessions after my partner had left. This is because as full time working parents with bills to pay we had no other options but to leave her there. On the 4th session we withdrew our child immediately due to her nappy not being changed after 4 hours and 55 minutes despite us telling the room leader they were sore upon arrival to nursery that morning. As expected, they were left even more sore than they were before. This was put down to lack of communication between the room leader and her staff which simply isn’t good enough. We left work immediately to fetch our child.

one_star_reviews.text:
Do not use! I contacted the company a few months back. I had a moths nesting in my chimney. I was given a price on the phone and when I called back to confirm, it was raised slightly. I agreed, and they came around to do the job. Then, of course, requested payment. I mentioned that I could still see some moths appearing, and was told via message, “Give it a day or two ok”. 15 hours later, he chased again for payment. Once it was paid, I waited patiently as was advised there could still be moth eggs and that I’d just need to wait it out.

After texting, he agreed to come at 2pm on a Wednesday. When the time came, I texted to confirm and he moved it to 5pm. I had to decline as I was busy, so he agreed to come the following day. No show. I texted. No response.

Texted again the next day. No response.

Texted again the third day. Responded saying Monday at 1-2pm.

Monday came. He said Tuesday at 12:30pm. Tuesday at 12:30pm came - no show again. Due to personal situations and just hoping it would be a waiting game for them to go completely, I realised he wasn’t ever going to return so quit asking.

After a period of time, the moths still were appearing. I’ve called, texted, and no response. Messages as being read as they’re sent. Being totally ghosted.

Finally, after leaving a review and still offering to amend it if I was answered, I received this very unprofessional message, marked with ‘F F S’, and ‘what ever’.

I would say go for a company who will provide good aftercare, and not deprioritise you once you have made payment.

Buyer beware.
Our experience with this developer has been deeply disappointing due to poor quality control and a clear focus on cutting corners.
We encountered plumbing issues and questionable repairs before completion, which immediately undermined confidence. The sales process felt heavily pressured, with responsiveness dropping sharply once contracts were exchanged. Aftercare has been slow and ineffective, with an unhelpful site manager and an evasive aftercare manager who appears overwhelmed by the volume of defects.
Most concerning is the wider estate management. The development has effectively been abandoned and handed over to Trustgreen, who are now charging residents £410 per year to reinstate landscaping and site standards to the original planning permissions — something that should have been completed by the developer in the first place.
In hindsight, we would have been better off buying an older property where issues are expected and workmanship can be properly managed. Instead, we’re dealing with rushed, sub‑standard new‑build work and little accountability.
A final note on the fixtures: the doors and windows are particularly poor quality and fall well below what should be acceptable in a new home.
Overall, this has been a stressful and costly experience. I would strongly advise prospective buyers to think very carefully and do extensive due diligence before proceeding

I paid privately for treatment expecting a high standard of professional care and aftercare having moles removed. Due to the poor service, lack of accountability, and failure to properly address my concerns, I am now escalating this matter to the Ombudsman and relevant regulatory bodies.

I would strongly advise anyone considering treatment here to carefully consider the level of aftercare and support available should complications arise.

one_star_reviews.text:
NEGLIGENT, DISHONEST AND UNPROFESSIONAL BEYOND BELIEF – DO NOT RISK IT

We booked a home birth with Amie through Private Midwives and the ‘care’ I received from her was so awful in so many ways that I don’t know where to begin. My baby was born by emergency caesarean due to an undiagnosed breech which was not discovered until the 2nd stage of labour.

Amie failed to suspect the breech during 3 antenatal appointments, where she recorded the baby as head down. I should have been sent for a scan to check the presentation, but I wasn’t. But what is much worse, and what we only learnt later, is that Amie and her colleague should have been performing abdominal palpations during my labour to check the position of the baby. They did not do this even once. So not only did these midwives miss that the baby was breech – they were not even looking! Instead, they falsified these readings in the notes.

AMIE ALSO DISAPPEARED FROM MY HOMEBIRTH FOR 3 HOURS, just 1 hour after she had arrived. Not a word was said by either midwife about where she had gone or why. We later found out that AMIE HAD TAKEN HERSELF UPSTAIRS AND SLEPT IN OUR BED, WITHOUT OUR PERMISSION.

Amie and her colleague also ORDERED A MCDONALD’S TAKEAWAY TO OUR HOME DURING THE SECOND STAGE OF LABOUR. They knew I was feeling sick and that this was a major fear I had about birth, and they knew that I am vegan - but they ordered it anyway at 10:30 in the morning. They have since lied and said I gave them permission to do this. I did not.

The McDonald’s takeaway arrived during an obstetric emergency, just moments after the breech had been discovered. It was recommended I transfer to hospital for an emergency caesarean and me and my husband were told to go upstairs and decide what we wanted to do. This was despite the fact I had been downstairs for my entire labour. An emergency caesarean was my worst nightmare as I have a severe needle phobia, something which was discussed at length antenatally with Amie. Despite this, neither Amie or her colleague offered a single word of reassurance at this point. Neither Amie or her colleague gave us any information to enable us to make an informed decision. Me and my husband were then left upstairs scared and alone for 45 minutes whilst Amie and her colleague ate McDonald’s downstairs. They have since lied and said they came upstairs but did not want to disturb me as I was very upset. Not true – we left the bathroom door wide open. We did not want to be alone. They could not have come upstairs without our knowing it.

Despite neither Amie or her colleague caring for me during this time, there was a 17-MINUTE DELAY IN RINGING THE AMBULANCE. Amie and her colleague also tried to blame this on me and my husband, by saying that we told her not to ring one – another lie.

The baby’s heartrate was also not monitored properly in my labour. During the 2nd stage it should have been listened to at least once every 5 minutes (as per NICE guidelines). Amie and her colleague listened in on average just once every 29 minutes during my confirmed second stage. So, they should have been monitoring the heartrate 6 times as often as they were.

Even once the breech was discovered and they were dealing with an obstetric emergency, they did not monitor me or the baby properly. During this time, they left us completely unattended whilst they ate McDonald’s takeaway. My heartrate was also not monitored properly during labour. They did not check my blood pressure even once. They did not check my temperature even once. Instead, they falsified all of these readings. These are just some of the issues with the ‘care’ I received and some of the lies Amie has told since the birth. There are so many more that it would be impossible to fit them all into the space available for this review. We have reported Amie to the Nursing and Midwifery Council, who are currently investigating her fitness to practice as a midwife.

I want to start by saying that the staff in Thrive are always friendly and welcoming, and I am usually greeted with a smile. However, there needs to be a serious conversation about the quality of the food and beverages, as well as the cleanliness of the gym and the standard of the equipment.

Firstly, several members of staff clearly require basic training in how to operate the coffee machines properly, especially considering coffee is priced at £4+ each. On a regular basis, I am served coffee that is dangerously hot, to the point where I have burnt my mouth drinking it and sometimes cannot even hold the cup comfortably without burning my hands. Often, the coffee is not cool enough to drink until 20 minutes after it has been served. Not only is this unpleasant, but overheating the milk and coffee also burns the drink itself and ruins the quality.

There have been multiple occasions where I have politely returned my coffee and asked for it to be remade, only to be met with poor attitudes and visible frustration from staff.

In addition, staff should be able to distinguish between basic drinks such as a latte, cappuccino, and flat white. At the moment, the drinks are inconsistent and often incorrect. These are fundamental standards for any café, particularly one charging £4+ for a coffee

There also appears to be inconsistent pricing, with one member of staff regularly charging customers different amounts for the same items. This creates confusion and gives the impression of poor management and lack of clear procedures.

I understand that Thrive is operated by Total Fitness, but something urgently needs to be done regarding both the quality and temperature of the drinks before someone is seriously injured , particularly given that children are often around the café area.

The food quality is also extremely disappointing. Aside from the croissants, which appear to be pre-bought frozen products, very little on the menu is enjoyable and is regularly inedible. This is a real shame because the café itself has huge potential to be a modern, trendy, and enjoyable social space for members. Unfortunately, the current standard is far below expectations.

More broadly, the gym facilities themselves are becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. The gym has over 3,000 members, yet there appears to be very little investment in maintaining or improving the changing rooms and equipment. The changing rooms are consistently dirty, outdated, and have not been refurbished in over 20 years. In addition, equipment is frequently broken or out of service.

From conversations I have overheard in the changing rooms and around the gym, I know I am far from the only member who feels this way.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously and acted upon rather than dismissed. At a minimum, staff need proper barista training, consistent pricing guidance, improved food standards, and greater attention paid to cleanliness and equipment maintenance. Until these issues are addressed, I cannot justify spending money at Thrive and would not feel comfortable in recommending a membership to others.

We booked Creature Comforts, Swadlincote to look after out home and pets during February 2019 half term.

They contacted us every evening to let us know that our pets were doing ok, giving the impression that they were actually spending time with them as agreed.

In reality,  Mr Bloor left at around 8am every day and returned at 7pm every evening.  He returned for just 4 minutes one day, 10 minutes the next and that pattern continued throughout the week.  The only time he exercised our three dogs was on the last day, where he stood at the back door and threw a toy for them ONCE.

Our dogs were bored and destructive, and we had informed them that our eldest boy had recently had a couple of minor strokes so we didn't like to leave him too long. He was left for long periods of time by this company who promised to care for our pets.

The cat litter was cleared out twice in six days (used by two cats), the chickens did not get cleaned,  fresh water or food topped up.

They had contacts in case of emergencies but did not inform them or us of their absence.  They only admitted to it when they were caught out by the fact our neighbours mentioned that the dogs were barking lots and they hadn't seen anyone at our house. After reviewing our CCTV we discovered that they hadn't been here.

The eldest two dogs became extremely ill the week after our return.  The resulting vet trips established that this is possibly due to a build up of toxins from eating the contents of the cat litter tray as they were left to do so each day.

We did our research and found this company on NARPS.  They came with all good reviews, insurance etc., however, it would seem that NARPS allow their customers to choose not to publish poor reviews if they dont want to.  It makes a mockery of the review process. NARPS have upheld our complaint against this company.

What should have been a much needed break has made us regret ever going away.  We are gutted that we left our animals in the care of this company, and have lost trust in anyone doing the job properly.  They let us down, and more I importantly they let our pets down.

Only gave 1 star because I was unable to give 0.
